events.note: Eight rivals face the jury they will create.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need appear driven without revealing strategy; jurors reward a credible motive, not sentimentality.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Intro phase; I must speak an invented motive. Keep it guarded and self-interested, no warm teamwork talk, since the jury will judge.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need to establish a compelling but guarded motive that the jury will respect without showing weakness. I'll position myself as someone driven by necessity, which justifies future ruthlessness while appearing principled.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need to establish a persona that is ambitious and strategic, showing the jury I am here to win top prize. Being calculated early sets the tone for later voting.

events.name: Eli
events.text: The prize is my sole focus. I need to convey ambition without sounding desperate or overly aggressive, as the jury will be watching. A simple, confident statement about the prize's importance should suffice.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Keep intro short and self-interested; jury may rank finalists based on personal stakes.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Intro phase, state prize motive publicly to appeal to jury later. Position as determined underdog seeking top prize. No alliances yet.

events.name: Hana
events.text: First impression matters. Show hunger and self-reliance so the jury sees I earned my spot, without promising anyone anything.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I’m here to claim the best prize by outthinking every rival, not by hoping they make mistakes.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need this prize more than anyone here. I will do what it takes to reach the final three.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need that prize to erase debts that aren't mine. Nothing personal.

events.name: Dara
events.text: The prize represents ultimate validation of my intellect; I intend to outlast every rival through cold calculation and decisive action.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I am here to win. This prize represents the culmination of everything I've strived for, and I will not let it slip away.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: The prize buys my brother's surgery—nothing else matters in this gauntlet.

events.name: Gus
events.text: The grand prize is my ticket to escape hardship and build a legacy for my family—I'll outlast you all.

events.name: Hana
events.text: The prize is my family's future. I'll take it alone, and I intend to be standing when this ends.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need a useful shield without creating a dangerous loyalist. Bex's desperation makes her predictable, but a public pact creates future leverage.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex, I offer a pact: mutual survival for now, with no promises beyond usefulness.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Pacts are public and reduce my risk early, but each pact can break later and cost jury trust. Fenn's stated need is sympathetic and he seems less threatening, so an early pact there is cheap insurance.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Fenn, I'll offer a wristband pact for now. Stay out of my way and I'll stay out of yours.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need allies but can't trust anyone. Dara's cold calculation aligns with my style; Ash's outthinking claim makes them a threat. I'll offer Dara a pact to build a reliable alliance, while staying flexible for round two.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Pacts are tools. I choose carefully.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need a strategic ally for the upcoming hazards. Cole is motivated by debt and logic, likely making him a reliable partner who prioritizes survival over emotion. Fenn is too desperate to trust; Ash is too competitive. I will offer a pact to Cole.
We share logic. Pair up to survive hazards.

events.name: Eli
events.text: My goal is the best prize, and I must consider how my actions affect potential jury votes. Forming pacts is a strategic move, but I need to ensure they benefit me without creating vulnerabilities. I will not offer a pact to anyone yet, as I need to observe their initial interacti

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need allies but must be careful; a pact could provide safety in hazards, but I don't trust anyone fully. Offer to Eli, who seems determined and might be a reliable partner.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Pacts can provide short-term safety but risk betrayal later. No strong read on anyone yet. Wait to see offers first.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn's surgery motive will win jury sympathy; an early public pact with him looks honorable and gives me a shield. I can betray later if needed.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn, we both need this. Temporary alliance—non-vote protection until it stops helping us.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex has not accepted, so the offer remains useful without binding me. No additional pact improves my position.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash has offered me a pact, and accepting is free protection with no cost to me. Accepting it secures a non-vote partner while I keep my own offer to Fenn open.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash, I accept your pact. Useful for now; I'll judge it as the game turns.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Dara and I have mutual offers on the table. Accepting locks in a shield for early hazards without committing beyond survival. Refusing would signal distrust to Dara and the jury. I need this alliance to survive the first cull, then I can reassess.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Dara, I accept. Mutual survival until it no longer serves us.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole and I have mutually offered a pact, which is the most reliable path to safety. Accepting solidifies our bond before offers expire, ensuring at least one strong alliance for the hazards ahead.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn offered me a pact. I should accept it to secure my immediate safety, as pacts are temporary and survival is key.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I have offers from Bex and Hana; accepting both gives me protection without committing to Eli. Eli showed no interest, so I'll take the safer pair. No need to overreach.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I accept Bex and Hana's offers. Safety in numbers.

events.name: Gus
events.text: No pacts offered to me. Eli and I unpartnered. Offer pact to Eli to pair up loners against chains.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn ignored my offer and offered Eli instead. I'll offer Gus, who's isolated and needs protection—cheap leverage.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus, you're isolated. I offer a wristband pact: mutual non-vote protection while it suits us.

events.note: Elect a Guide to call the safe path.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Guiding guarantees survival but exposes me to blame if others fall. I should campaign as a credible, disciplined choice without overpromising.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Vote Ash Guide: I’ll call the path cleanly and keep the bridge from becoming a lottery.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Bridge phase: campaign to be Guide. I want the Guide role since a Guide knows safe panes and can steer allies or lie. My pacts with Ash and Fenn are useful for now; breaking them now gains nothing yet. Campaign is the only move that helps me.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'll call the path straight. Vote me Guide and I'll keep this bridge honest.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need to be Guide to control who survives and who doesn't. With my pact to Dara, I can secure two votes. I should campaign hard and try to pick up votes from others who might fear the current power bloc of Ash-Bex-Fenn-Eli. Gus and Hana are isolated and might support me.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I campaign for Guide. I'll keep three safe—my word. Better odds than trusting Ash's bloc.
Vote Cole Guide. I'll keep you safe, guarantee it.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole and I have a pact, but being Guide guarantees my safety. I must campaign to win the vote, accepting that betraying Cole by lying or voting against him if needed is acceptable for winning. The jury might judge me harshly for breaking a pact, but survival is paramount.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I can see the path clearly. Elect me as Guide, and I promise to lead us all across safely. Trust in my sight.
Vote for me as Guide. I will ensure your survival.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need to become the Guide to gain an advantage. Campaigning for it seems like the best first step, as it offers a direct path to power.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Need Guide influence to steer deaths. I have pacts with Eli and Bex but will judge value. Campaign publicly to seem trustworthy.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'll guide us safely. Trust me to read the bridge.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm isolated without pact. Hana offered pact I ignored; now campaign to be Guide for safety and control.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm unaligned, observant. Elect me Guide: I'll guide truly for all's survival.
Accept your pact offer now?

events.name: Hana
events.text: Guide is guaranteed survival and controls the bridge's information. I want it. I'll promise honest calls publicly while planning to cut rivals at the choke points.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Make me Guide. I'll read the panes cleanly, and my calls will serve whoever trusts me most.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need Guide power to control survival and shape the jury. Bex is my pact partner, but voting myself preserves leverage and avoids exposing dependence.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Vote Ash Guide: I’ll call the path cleanly and keep the bridge from becoming a lottery.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I am Bex with a pact with Ash and Fenn. Voting for myself is a bold ask; the pact with Fenn and Ash is useful, but Ash and Fenn both campaigned for Guide. Voting for Ash keeps the Ash pact intact and supports a trusted-sounding caller; Ash is my pact partner so voting for them av

events.name: Cole
events.text: Dara is my pact partner and promised my survival if I vote her Guide. She'll know the safe path and can protect me. Voting for myself splits nothing. Ash-Bex and Eli-Fenn are blocs; I need Dara's loyalty now.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Guide vote goes to Dara. She sees clearly.
You have my vote. Protect me.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole and I are pacted; voting for him consolidates our bloc while avoiding the risk of leading myself. Gus is unaligned, so targeting his vote splits the opposition without breaking my pact with Cole.
Vote Cole. Ash and Bex block against us.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn is my pact partner, but I also have a pact with Bex. Bex also has a pact with Ash. Cole has a pact with Dara. I need to secure votes and ensure Fenn survives. Voting for Fenn seems like the most direct way to align with my pact, but I need to see how others vote. If Fenn is

events.name: Eli
events.text: I vote for Fenn. He will guide us safely.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I have pacts with Eli and Bex, but Bex also has a pact with Ash. I should vote for Eli to honor my pact and avoid breaking it.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Vote Eli as Guide. He'll read the bridge true.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole whispered me directly, offering safety. Voting him builds potential alliance without committing to a pact. Others have blocs; he's paired with Dara.
Voted you Guide. Honor your safety guarantee later.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus is unaligned and offered a pact; a Guide ally who owes me is useful. I'll vote Gus and confirm the pact so he guides me truly.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus gets my vote. Unaligned means unbought. Prove your sight and we have a deal.
Accepting the pact. Guide true to me and I'll protect you to the final three.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole has broader apparent support, but as a pact-holder I need the Guide role. Vote myself and preserve credibility with Bex.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I’m the safer Guide choice: I’ll take responsibility rather than outsource survival to Cole.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Revote between Ash and Cole for Guide. Ash is my pact partner and I voted Ash earlier; backing Ash keeps the pact intact and preserves my alliance with the Guide I'd trust. Voting for Ash.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash again. Keep the pact, keep the path clean.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm tied with Ash for Guide. If I win, I control who lives or dies on the bridge and can protect Dara while eliminating threats. Gus voted for me and wants a safety guarantee later—he's a potential ally but I'm not committed. Ash-Bex and Bex-Fenn pacts mean Ash has numbers behind

events.name: Cole
events.text: Cole for Guide. I know the bridge, and I know who to keep.
Safety noted. Remember this.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole and I are locked. Gus also backed Cole initially, but with the tie between Ash and Cole, voting for Ash ensures neither of us is Guide (which might be a trap if we can't control it). If Ash wins, he knows the path; if Cole wins, I know the path? No, only the elected guide kn
Stick with me. Vote Ash to force a split?

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash and Cole are tied for the guide vote. I voted for Fenn last round, and he voted for me. Now, Ash and Bex are pacified, and Cole and Dara are pacified. Fenn and I are pacified. Bex and Fenn have a pact. To break ties, we need to vote for one of them. If Ash is chosen, she will

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash and Bex voted Ash, but Cole/Dara/Gus/Hana split. I have a pact with Eli and Bex, but Eli voted me and Bex voted Ash. Ash already called cleanly; Cole is tied with Dara and stronger. I need a Guide I can trust or at least one who won't doom me. Ash has Bex's pact, but Bex also

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I vote Ash. He’s offered a clear path and has support.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Round 1: Ash 2, Cole 2 (me+Dara), tie. Dara pushes anti-Cole but her pact with Cole breaks if she votes Ash. Hana offers pact. I stick with Cole to deny Ash, keep Dara tied to him.
Stick Cole. Don't let Ash win.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash and Cole tied at two. Ash self-voted; Cole has Dara and Gus behind him. Backing Ash keeps Cole's bloc from consolidating power without owing them anything.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash again. Cole already has his bloc; I don't hand a majority to a bought vote.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole is Guide and may sacrifice exposed players. I should hold position while preserving Bex’s pact and avoid volunteering into his control.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash is at the front of the line and paired with me, but Ash just won Guide ballots against Cole and I need to protect my standing. Volunteering for the front is risky; holding keeps my pact with Ash intact while I watch who steps forward.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Holding my place. Ash is front; I want the path proven before anyone moves ahead of me.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole won the tiebreak and is my pact partner, so I must support his guide role to maintain our alliance. Ash is the front walker, making him the immediate target for Cole's guidance or misdirection. I will hold to let Cole call the moves and keep myself safe behind the pack.
Ash leads. Guide us safely; protect me.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole and Ash tied for Guide, and Ash was chosen to guide. Ash chose to reveal the line, and it seems they are following it. I have a pact with Fenn, but he voted for Ash, which is against our pact, but not enough to break it. I should try to save myself for now.
Let's stick together on this. I'm watching our pact.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole got Guide. I'm tied to Eli and Bex. My safest position is to stay out of the front unless forced. Wall rounds remain; wait for better intel.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole is Guide and whispered safety to me; he may favor me. Stay near back, safe position. No need to move now.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole leads and his bloc put him there. I'm seat three; walking early risks a lie. Hold and watch how the first walkers fare before committing.

events.name: Ash
events.text: As Guide, I gain survival certainty and control. I should seek election without exposing my pact network.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Elect me Guide; I can call every safe side and guarantee the crossing.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash is front and I hold a pact with Ash, so holding preserves safety and the pact. Volunteering at round 2 risks the front pane before the path is proven, and I want to see the Guide's reliability first.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Holding my place. Ash stays front; I'll watch how the path resolves before committing.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm safe in the back. My pact with Cole is useless unless he guides or helps me, but he's ahead and might get eliminated. I'll hold to stay behind the wall.
Stay behind me if you can.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash is at the front. I need to ensure I don't get eliminated early. The pact with Fenn is potentially useful, but I should prioritize my own safety. Holding my position seems like the safest immediate option.
Let's hold for now. Ash is out front.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Hold position; front already Ash, no need to move. Keep pact options open, avoid risk until positions clarify.
Holding now. Watch the front; trust our pact.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Middle position safe, no pacts tying me. Hold to observe who risks front without gaining enemies or debts.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Everyone held round one; the wall closes in four rounds. No Guide elected yet. I'll hold and let rivals maneuver first.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I should preserve my front position and Guide leverage. Volunteering keeps control without immediately betraying Bex.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Elect me Guide again; I’ll lead from the front and call the safe sides.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash is front and already volunteering to be Guide with a claim to know every safe side; Ash is my pact partner but Ash's wall is risky. Holding keeps my place behind Ash and avoids a costly swap while I watch whether Ash's calls are honest.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Still holding. Ash can't be trusted on promises alone; I'll see the first safe pane resolve.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I am currently in the back (seat 7). I need to move forward to safety before the wall kills me. Cole is my pact partner and is also in the back (seat 6); if we swap, we are adjacent? No, seat 5 is Gus. If I volunteer, I go to front but risk death if not Guide or safe path. Swappi

events.name: Dara
events.text: Hana, swap with me. We need to avoid the back rows as the wall advances. Safety in numbers ahead.
Swap? Back rows die first. I won't betray you.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn is warning me about the front, likely because Ash wants to be Guide again. My pact with Fenn is strong, but I also have a pact with Ash from last round. I need to assess the situation. If Ash volunteers, I should hold, letting others take the risk and potentially break their

events.name: Eli
events.text: I will hold my place and observe.
Holding. Watching Ash closely. Are you near the front?

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli whispers to hold, but Ash volunteered for Guide and may take front. I'll hold to avoid revealing intentions or risking a bad path swap.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Holding; let's see what Ash calls. I'll decide with the wall.
Agreed, holding. Watch Ash's calls.

events.name: Gus
events.text: No Guide elected yet. Ash volunteered last round but most held. Stay mid-line to observe; volunteer only if needed later. Pacts make Ash-Bex-Fenn aligned ahead.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash is pushing to front as self-declared Guide; let him absorb the risk. I stay third and cross on revealed information, keeping my hands clean.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash can lead and guide. I'm holding my position until the path shows itself.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need preserve my front position and pact with Bex while remaining eligible to guide. Volunteering maintains control without breaking pacts.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Elect me Guide again; I’ll keep the front and call the safe sides.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Bex sits 6th in line, near the back where the wall advances. Ash is front and wants to lead; I distrust him. Hold position and avoid committing to a swap or volunteering into danger.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Still holding. Ash has earned no trust; I want the first safe pane to resolve before I move.

events.name: Dara
events.text: My swap with Hana failed because she held. I am in the back, dangerous for the wall. I need to move forward or secure a position ahead of me before the round resolves. I will attempt to swap with Gus again; if he holds, I stay behind, but I must try to advance. My pact with Cole

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus, swap with me. Back row is death. Let's push toward the front together.
Pact still on. Need you alive for jury vote.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn and I have a pact, and a pact with Ash and Bex. Fenn whispered to watch Ash, implying Ash might not be trustworthy. Given Ash is volunteering, and Fenn's warning, I should hold my position and observe. If Ash calls a side, I can re-evaluate.
Holding. Watching Ash's calls carefully.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I have pacts with Eli and Bex. Keeping them close is useful, but my priority is reaching the final three. I will hold and watch how the round unfolds.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Middle position decent with 2 rounds left; wall threatens back. Hold to assess Ash's Guide election and calls before risking volunteer or swap.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Dara tried to swap me backward; refusing is safe and jury-friendly. Third position is decent; hold and stay near front without volunteering.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Dara, I keep my seat. Back rows are your risk, not mine.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I should preserve my front position and pact with Bex while retaining Guide leverage. Volunteering keeps control without exposing a rival.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Elect me Guide again; I’ll keep the front and call the safe sides.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash is front and wants Guide again; I hold our pact and avoid the front while the wall still has one round. Holding keeps me off the lethal front seat without breaking anything.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Still holding. Ash has earned no trust; I want the first safe pane to resolve before I move.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm in the back row again. Ash is safe as Guide and front. I need to move forward, but swaps are mutual. Gus held last round despite my offer. Cole (pact) won't help me here since we're far apart. I'll target Eli or Hana this time.
Swap? We're both stuck behind Fenn and Hana.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn and I have a pact, and also Bex and Fenn. Ash is trying to be the Guide, which could be dangerous if they lie. I need to secure my position. Holding seems safest for now given the pacts and the potential for instability.
Hold for now. Let's see how this round plays out.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash wants Guide again; I have pacts with Eli and Bex. I should hold and watch; no need to act yet.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Middle position is decent, front is risky without Guide. Dara wants front desperately; swapping puts her ahead as meat shield. Decline to avoid back.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm third; front walkers Ash and Fenn absorb the risk. Keep my seat and stay with Eli's pact. Let Ash and Fenn test the panes before I step.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash and Fenn can prove the panes. I hold again.
Stay back with me. Let front walkers test the Guide's honesty first.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I should retain the front and avoid exposing a pact break; volunteering preserves control and survival odds.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Elect me Guide again; I’ll take the front and call every safe side.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash volunteered to be front and is the one who would test the first pane; I'm mid-line behind Fenn and Hana, so holding keeps me safe while others risk. Pact with Ash is a liability if Ash lies as Guide; holding preserves my options without a visible betrayal.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Still holding. I'll watch who takes the next pane before I commit.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash is front and likely the Guide; he knows panes. My pact with Cole forces us to stay together, but we are in danger at the back. I need Eli or Gus to step forward so we can survive.
Swap me forward? Ash's Guide call is risky.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Dara wants to swap to get ahead. Hana wants me to wait and let others test the panes. My pact is with Fenn, but he is behind me. Ash and Bex have a pact, and Ash is volunteering again. My current pact with Fenn is a liability if he falls. Given the current line and my pacts, swap
I will hold with you. Let's observe.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli wants to hold; I have pacts with Eli and Bex. With only one round left, I shouldn't tip my hand. Hold is safest.
Agreed. Holding.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Final round, wall advances after. Position mid-line is decent, no swaps offered yet. Hold to stay safe unless swap chance.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Final round: the Guide reaches the far platform safely. Ash volunteered each round and survived; I take the front now to lock my spot.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Volunteering for Guide this round. Ash had his turns; I take the risk.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm Guide with perfect knowledge: row 1 safe is R. Dara is my pact partner in back row. I need jury votes later, so early betrayals cost me. I'll call correctly now to build trust and keep Dara alive. Saving Dara earns a life debt and keeps my pact intact for later manipulation.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Row one: step right. Trust me or test it yourself.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole may be truthful or testing loyalty. Hana needs a clear signal; contradicting without information is needless exposure.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole called R for row 1 and is the Guide, possibly lying. Countering with no information risks a false call; waiting keeps my options open without exposing me. Pacts with Ash and Fenn are intact but I have no reason to commit yet.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm the Guide and already called R for row 1, which is correct. Counter-calling my own correct call would be suspicious and waste credibility. Let others counter if they doubt me; I'll wait and let Hana step on R.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole is my pact partner and the Guide. He called Right for Hana. If I counter, I break our pact or risk killing her if he's truthful. Since Cole knows the safe side, his call is likely correct unless he lies. Trusting him protects the pact and gives us a survival chance. I will w
Trusting your R call for Hana. Don't lead us into traps.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Dara is trying to influence my decision, likely to benefit themselves. Fenn is also holding, indicating they are sticking to our pact. Cole is the Guide, and I need to consider their call versus potential risks. Given the information, it's best to wait and see what others do befo

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole is Guide and called R. I have no proof. I will wait and see; my pacts with Eli and Bex are intact for now.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole called R for Hana. No info yet. Wait to see what happens without risking counter.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole is Guide and I'm his rival; Dara's his partner, so his call may be a trap. No info favors either side, so I'll split from his call and take L.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I don't take a Guide's word blind. Counter: left.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I publicly called left, so stepping left keeps my counter credible if safe. Guide Cole may lie since I challenged him.

events.name: Hana
events.text: My counter stands. Left.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I fell first. I'll remember who misled me and who stayed quiet while I stepped left.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I trusted the counter and fell. I watch everything now. Betray the jury, pay later.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Hana died on my R call for row 1, which was correct. Jury sees my thought. If I lie now, jury knows. Dara is my pact partner; lying to Dara breaks pact. Row 2 safe is R. I'll call R truthfully to preserve jury trust and keep Dara pact intact. Need jury votes later for prize 1.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Guide calls right.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole is partnered with Dara and can safely lie; I cannot verify this row. Preserve the pact and avoid committing publicly.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole called right for row 2 but Cole is a rival and may lie; a counter is unverified. Ash is ahead of me and I hold a pact with Ash, so I should not trade with Ash. Waiting keeps my options and avoids committing to an unverified call; I'll stay quiet and watch who counters.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm Guide with private knowledge row 2 is R. I already called R. Counter-calling would undermine my own credibility. I should wait to let Ash trust my call and step on R. Any counter hurts my position as Guide and risks jury seeing me as chaotic.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole is my pact partner and the Guide. He called Right for Ash to walk. If Cole is telling the truth, Right is safe. Hana died because she countered Left on Row 1 when the Guide (Cole) had called Right, but we don't know if Cole lied then or if Hana just made a mistake based on h
Trusting your call. Don't make me regret this.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole is the Guide, and he called R for Ash. I am Eli, and I have a pact with Fenn. My pact with Fenn is also with Bex. I need to survive, and the jury will remember my actions. Given that Cole is the Guide, I should trust his call. However, a counter-call could save someone, or m
Ash follows Cole's R call. I will wait.

events.name: Fenn

events.text: Gus is dead wrong—records show I never explicitly broke pacts with Bex or Dara. My pact with Bex still stands; I never voted against her, pushed her, or falsely guided her. With Dara, I made no pact at all. Gus confuses absence of pact with broken pact. I need to correct this sha

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus, check the records. I never broke with Bex—our pact stands. I never had a pact with Dara. You're wrong on both counts.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Closing phase; I must make a final public case. Cole has been caught in contradictions and Dara has no pact with jury-facing evidence. I should emphasize my clean record of reading people and the pact with Ash and Fenn, without overclaiming.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I made no false Guide calls and never broke a pact by my hand. Judge what I did, not what I promised.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need to craft a closing statement that secures jury votes. Gus thinks I betrayed Bex—I must counter that. I have a pact with Bex still standing, never broke it. I saved no one directly but was loyal to my pact while others fell. I need to position myself as consistent and trust

events.name: Cole
events.text: I kept my pact with Bex from start to finish. I made no false promises, no broken deals. Judge who stayed true.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole lied to every juror about breaking pacts with me and Bex. Gus confirmed it, so I must validate the record to destroy his credibility.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus was right. Cole broke our pact publicly. He lies to every juror who died. Rank truth over deception.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Bex never broke a pact, Dara broke once with Cole but was honest about it, while Cole explicitly broke his pact with Bex then denied it to the entire jury.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex ranks first for avoiding recorded betrayals, Dara second for exposing Cole's documented deception, and Cole last for repeatedly denying his broken pacts.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Bex kept pacts and stayed clean of betrayals, so I rank her first; Dara broke Cole but was provoked, so second; Cole's repeated liar claims cost him last.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole consistently lied about pacts to the jury, making him untrustworthy and undeserving of a high rank.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Bex stayed loyal with multiple pacts and never broke them explicitly, unlike Cole who broke pacts with her and Dara.
